name: assembly-shortfall-shape
description: The chain-assembly binding shortfall is NEITHER an extensivity failure NOR a coefficient. B_model is affine in (Z,N) (exactly A-1 bonds) so B/A converges to -(alpha/2)ln(f_pp*f_nn) and model/AME is bounded below by 0.307 across A=2..238 -- not extensivity. B_model/A is strictly increasing along N=Z and bounded by its limit while AME B/A peaks at 62Ni and falls, so no positive constant reproduces the fall, and the deuteron refuses a uniform factor 3 outright -- not a coefficient. The missing shape is the Z(Z-1) Coulomb multiplicity that CrossingCountAffine proves the crossing counts cannot supply. Scope (a) for the numbers, (b) for the monotonicity exclusion.

assertions.name: model B/A converges to the closed-form limit
assertions.detail: |B/A - limit| falls monotonically to 0.000301533 at A=10^4; limit = 2.924246313761893507377392 MeV/nucleon (exact closed form)

assertions.name: model/AME does NOT decay -- bounded away from 0, with an interior minimum near the AME peak
assertions.detail: the ratio bottoms at 0.3068193 (4He, A=4) and RISES to 0.41079556 (238U, A=238); never below 0.3068193 anywhere. An extensivity deficit would send it monotonically to 0. It does the opposite past A~60 -- see section 7.

assertions.name: B_model is affine in (Z,N) -- exactly A-1 bonds, no curvature
assertions.detail: both second differences vanish (0.0, 0.0) -- so B_model/A tends to a constant and the model has the extensive A-scaling already

assertions.name: the AME side has NO asymptote -- B/A rises, peaks, falls
assertions.detail: peak at A=62 (8.7945555 MeV/nucleon), down to 7.5701262 at A=238. So there is no constant to divide by: '3' is a ratio to the PEAK, not to a limit.

assertions.name: 3x agreement is a CROSSING, not a plateau -- not evidence for 3
assertions.detail: 3*model/AME is 0.99944857 at 40Ca (A=40) but 1.4010365 at 7Li (A=7). A constant-B/A model can only CROSS a rising-peaking-falling curve; it crosses near the peak. Same trap as R3 and qou-vudb.

assertions.name: the constant is NEAR 3 but is not measurably 3
assertions.detail: k = 3.00746057492204, |k - 3| = 0.0074605749 (0.248686%). Near 3, and the comparison point (the empirical peak) is not a fundamental quantity, so this cannot be sharpened by measuring harder.

assertions.name: a UNIFORM factor 3 is refuted by the deuteron (scope (a))
assertions.detail: the single-bond nucleus is already OVER-bound by the bare model (1.2735798x); tripling puts it at 3.8207394x AME. So whatever supplies the factor near 3 at large A must VANISH at A=2 -- it is not a uniform per-bond multiplicity.

assertions.name: the model's B/A is MONOTONE and the data's is PEAKED -- a shape mismatch, not a coefficient one
assertions.detail: B_model/A increases strictly in A along N=Z and is bounded above by 2.92424631376, so it can NEVER turn over. AME B/A turns over at A=62. Rescaling the model by ANY positive constant preserves monotonicity, so no choice of the constant in section 5 reproduces the fall -- which is why model/AME rises again past A~60 in section 2, instead of settling.
